spatial_entity.notes: Reuses the existing reviewed Uruk spatial identity and reviewed geometry. The claim is institutionally bounded and must not be inflated to all inhabitants or all Old Babylonian cities.

claim.date_text_original: Rīm-Anum's short reign at Uruk, 1742–1740 BCE
claim.summary: Texts from the Old Babylonian bīt asīrī at Uruk under Rīm-Anum document prisoners of war used as a labour force and as slaves within a state-managed institutional setting connected with flour production. This supports a bounded positive slavery designation at Uruk for this short period, but not a city-wide prevalence estimate or a claim that every prisoner or worker was enslaved.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim 6d4a714b-1899-440f-b8c2-7c2b8b1d2cc9. Legacy P3 is not copied into this post-M1 claim.

territorial_practice.notes: Bounded institutional presence only; no prevalence or all-Uruk intensity inference.

source.title: From Freedom to Slavery: Work and Words at the House of Prisoners of War in the Old Babylonian Period
source.temporal_scope: Old Babylonian period, especially Rīm-Anum's reign
source.independence_notes: Dedicated specialist study of the Uruk bīt asīrī source corpus.
source.reliability_limitations: Institution-specific corpus; cannot by itself establish city-wide slave prevalence or homogeneous status for all war captives.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist interpretation of the bīt asīrī institutional corpus
evidence.locator: abstract and article analysis of prisoners of war used as labour force and slaves
